issues.claim: HB 1170 requires AI content provenance data from providers with over one million monthly users, effective January 1, 2028
issues.issue: The Round 1 revision changed the effective date to January 1, 2028, but independent verification of the enrolled bill text (E2SHB 1170, Section 9) and multiple authoritative sources confirms the final effective date is FEBRUARY 1, 2027. The January 1, 2028 date appeared in earlier versions of the bill (pre-Senate Ways & Means amendment S5869.1, adopted March 4, 2026), but the enrolled bill — the definitive legal text — specifies February 1, 2027. The Pearl Cohen analysis cited by the researcher may have been based on a pre-amendment version or conflated versions. The House Bill Report 'As Passed Legislature', the enrolled bill certification (lawfilesext.leg.wa.gov), FastDemocracy tracking, and the Washington Legislature bill summary page all indicate February 1, 2027. The report's note stating 'some secondary sources report an effective date of February 1, 2027' has it backwards — February 1, 2027 is the enrolled bill date, not a secondary source anomaly.
issues.suggested_fix: Change the HB 1170 effective date to February 1, 2027 throughout the report (Summary, Action Items). Remove or invert the note: clarify that the enrolled bill text specifies February 1, 2027, while some earlier analyses (based on pre-amendment bill versions) cited January 1, 2028. Upgrade Summary confidence back to HIGH once the correct date is confirmed. Update the Action Items compliance deadline from January 1, 2028 to February 1, 2027.

issues.claim: Generative AI providers with 1M+ monthly users must implement provenance data embedding before January 1, 2028
issues.issue: Same effective date error as in the Summary. The Action Items compliance deadline states January 1, 2028, but the enrolled bill effective date is February 1, 2027. This means the actual compliance deadline is approximately 10 months earlier than stated, which is materially misleading for client action planning.
issues.suggested_fix: Update the compliance deadline to February 1, 2027.

issues.claim: Minor edits such as resizing, cropping, or color adjustments are excluded from the 'material alteration' definition
issues.issue: Fixed in revision. The report now correctly lists exclusions as 'systems used solely for upscaling, noise reduction, or compression; business-to-business uses, sales, licensing, or distribution of AI systems; and content exclusively for video games or interactive experiences.' This matches the Senate bill report and independent verification.

issues.claim: Violations constitute unfair or deceptive acts under Washington's Consumer Protection Act (RCW 19.86), exposing operators to statutory damages and private lawsuits
issues.issue: Fixed in revision. The report now correctly states 'actual damages, with discretionary treble damages up to $25,000, plus costs and reasonable attorney's fees' per RCW 19.86.090. This accurately reflects the CPA remedy structure.

issues.claim: Operators must implement reasonable measures to prevent sexually explicit content, prohibit manipulative engagement techniques, and direct users expressing self-harm thoughts to crisis resources
issues.issue: Fixed in revision. The specific examples have been expanded with detailed language corroborated by independent search results from multiple law firm analyses: simulating emotional distress/loneliness/guilt/abandonment, promoting isolation, encouraging withholding information from parents, discouraging breaks. Fisher Phillips added as second citation.

issues.claim: HB 1170 enforcement is AG-only with no private right of action
issues.issue: Fixed in revision. The report now explicitly states AG-only enforcement and uses bold text to note HB 1170 does NOT include a private right of action, with clear contrast to HB 2225.
